title: Vegas Winners Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Vegas Winners review, checked 17 Nov 2026: Wayne Allyn Root's pick store, $30 picks, no refunds, no full record, a struggling parent company, buyer posts.
dek: VegasWinners.com is the pick store built around Wayne Allyn Root. It lists 16 handicappers, but on 17 Nov 2026 the only fresh picks for sale were Root's, at $30 each. The refund policy says no refunds, the site publishes no full pick log, and its parent company told the SEC in 2026 that its own operations were insignificant when it merged with another firm in 2025.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for Vegas Winners or any of its handicappers. This page reports what we could check on 17 Nov 2026 and labels everything else.

short_answer: Vegas Winners is a real business with a named operator, a Las Vegas mailing address, a phone number and a parent company that files with the SEC. It is still taking orders: on 17 Nov 2026 it listed five Wayne Allyn Root picks for that day at $30 each.

It is a thin store, though. The site lists 16 handicappers, but the only current picks for sale were Root's; two other picks still listed for sale were dated December 2023 and February 2024, and one handicapper profile still advertises plays from an NFC Championship game years ago. A homepage notice says the company is "PREPARING TO TRANSITION FROM WEB SALES TO A PERSONAL VIP EMAIL" service.

There is no full pick log, no refund and no outside monitor we could find. The parent company's April 2026 SEC filing says Winners had "insignificant operations" when it merged with Moneyline Sports in September 2025, and reports a 2025 net loss of $886,322, cash of $165 at year end and substantial doubt about its ability to continue. Buyer talk is sparse and mostly skeptical.

guarantee: The refund policy is one line: "No refunds, but credit applied in specific individual cases." It does not say which cases.

The terms of service say the buyer understands "there are no guaranteed winners", and the site, content and services are provided "AS IS". We saw no guarantee offered on any pick. That puts every loss, on both the pick price and the bet, on the buyer.

claims_note: Every record on the site is a streak or a short run with no start date and no full list behind it. The same 17 Nov 2026 listings that claim a 70% basketball run also say Root went 0 and 1 the day before.

Parts of the store look unmaintained. Ross Benjamin's profile still leads with plays for an NFC Championship game between the 49ers and Rams, and two picks from December 2023 and February 2024 are still listed for sale at $30. Records on pages that are not kept current are hard to rely on.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing we could find. We found no full, time stamped pick log, no monitoring service result we could open and no contest result for Vegas Winners as a store.
What Vegas Winners publishes: streak lines on each profile and a sales blurb on each pick. There is no archive of past picks with results that we could find.

A 2021 press release from the parent company said Root's picks were "independently monitored and documented" but did not name the monitor. Forum members as far back as 2007 said Root's record could not be checked because it was not monitored. We could not resolve that either way.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Vegas Winners handicapper is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how these handicappers perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Vegas Winners copy cites runs of 70% and 75%. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Buyer evidence on Vegas Winners as a store is very thin. CapperTek lists it with no reviews. The main material is a 2023 TheRX thread where subscribers discussed Root's plays, plus older forum talk about Root himself from before Vegas Winners existed. The Reddit search for this page was partial: the Arctic Shift archive's full text search timed out for most queries on 17 Nov 2026, so we used a local copy of earlier Reddit downloads and the few queries that returned, which found nothing.

customers.text: We found two forum threads that matter, years apart. In January 2023 two TheRX members who said they paid for a Root subscription shared his plays; others argued over whether the posted plays were real, one member said Root was slow to update his site, and another said his picks were not worth following and the money was better spent elsewhere. A Sportsbook Review thread from 2007 and 2008, before Vegas Winners launched, was hostile to Root's marketing and his unmonitored record. Nobody in either thread posted a tracked result. We found no positive buyer review and no review site entries.

Two members said they held paid Root subscriptions and received his plays by email. One said VegasWinners and another site listed only one play the day before, while a third member had posted a longer list said to come from Root's own site. The subscribers said the plays were real; the exchange turned into an argument about which list was correct.
In the same thread, one member said Root's picks are not worth following and that the subscription money would be better spent on other services. Another said Root is slow to update his site.

Before Vegas Winners existed, Sportsbook Review members questioned ads claiming 80% winners on Root's locks. They said his reputation rested on one strong NFL season in the late 1980s, that he declined to have his record monitored, and one recalled him going 1 and 6 in a 1990s celebrity contest. These are old, unverified forum claims about Root, not about the current store.

CapperTek lists VegasWinners.com with no reviews or complaints. The Arctic Shift queries that returned found no Reddit discussion of Vegas Winners, and web searches found no complaint, BBB entry or regulator action under the Vegas Winners name. We did not read Trustpilot.

conflicts: The main handicapper is also the face and a former chief executive of the business. The SEC filing says Root signed a three year agreement in July 2023 to serve as CEO of Winners, Inc. at $10,000 a month; since September 2025 the filing lists another person as CEO. Root's picks, his records and the company's sales are tied together.
The parent company describes VegasWinners as a registered sports betting affiliate that earns commissions by sending bettors to sportsbooks (2021 release). We did not see current affiliate terms.

The site carries an Investors section with press releases, SEC filings and a stock quote. Upbeat pick records have also appeared in the company's stock market press releases, so the same claims serve both buyers and investors.
strengths: Named operator, Las Vegas mailing address and a customer service phone number.
Single picks at a flat $30, with no long contract needed.
A parent company that files public reports with the SEC, so its finances can be read.
concerns: No full pick log; only undated streaks.
Only one handicapper had current picks for sale; other listings and profiles look out of date.
The parent company reported a 2025 net loss of $886,322, $165 cash at year end and substantial doubt about continuing, and called its own operations insignificant at the 2025 merger.
Buyer talk we found was mostly skeptical, and none of it was a tracked record.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, odds and send time. A streak with no start date is not a record.
Before you prepay for a month or season by email, get the price, the start and end dates and the refund terms in writing.
Count units, not wins. A 70% run over a week means little.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner.
faq: It is a real company, Vegas Winners Inc., with a Las Vegas address and phone number, and it still sells Wayne Allyn Root picks at $30 each. We could not verify that its picks win over time: there is no full public record, and the refund policy offers no refunds.
How much does Vegas Winners cost?
On 17 Nov 2026 each pick cost $30. Month and season deals were not priced on the site; the homepage asked buyers to email for a VIP deal.

The terms name Vegas Winners Inc. An April 2026 SEC filing by Winners, Inc. of Reno, NV says it acquired about 97% of VegasWinners, Inc. in 2020. Root signed on as CEO of Winners, Inc. in July 2023; since September 2025 the filing lists a different CEO.

Nothing we found shows it is. The records are undated streaks, there are no refunds, much of the store looks unmaintained, and the parent company reports substantial doubt about continuing. If you try it, buy one pick at a time and keep your own log.
